D=/scr/wurgaft/auto-psych/agent_trees/fc3d1e4e3afb1c37/repo/_runs/cell_1/experiment1/model_loop/iter_0/critique/test_stats
mkdir -p $D; rm -f $D/*.py
cat << 'EOF' > $D/example_target_yes_rate.py
# name: example_target_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate on trials where the target is itself one of the shown examples; t_observed below null_mean means people endorse shown examples less than the model (which predicts near-certain yes).
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).astype(str)
    padded = "," + s.str.replace(" ", "", regex=False) + ","
    m = np.array([("," + b + ",") in a for a, b in zip(padded.values, t.values)])
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].values[m].mean())
EOF
cat << 'EOF' > $D/single_example_yes_rate.py
# name: single_example_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate among trials whose set has exactly one example (target not equal to it); t_observed above null_mean means people generalize more broadly from one example than the model does.
def test_statistic(df):
    n = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.count(",") + 1
    first = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",").str[0].astype(int)
    m = (n == 1) & (first != df["target"].astype(int))
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"][m].mean())
EOF
cat << 'EOF' > $D/early_minus_late_yes_rate.py
# name: early_minus_late_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate in the first third of trial_index minus yes rate in the last third; a nonzero t_observed vs null_mean (~0) means response bias drifts over the session, which the model cannot produce.
def test_statistic(df):
    ti = df["trial_index"].astype(float)
    lo, hi = ti.quantile(1/3), ti.quantile(2/3)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    a, b = r[ti <= lo], r[ti >= hi]
    if len(a) == 0 or len(b) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(a.mean() - b.mean())
EOF
cat << 'EOF' > $D/far_target_yes_rate.py
# name: far_target_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate for targets more than 25 away from every example in the set; t_observed above null_mean means people give more distant/rule-based (or noise) yeses than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    u = pd.unique(sets)
    arr = {k: np.array([int(x) for x in k.split(",")]) for k in u}
    tgt = df["target"].astype(int).values
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(sets)
    d = np.empty(len(df))
    for i, k in enumerate(uniq):
        idx = codes == i
        d[idx] = np.abs(tgt[idx][:, None] - arr[k][None, :]).min(axis=1)
    m = d > 25
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].values[m].mean())
EOF
cat << 'EOF' > $D/near_target_yes_rate.py
# name: near_target_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets within 1-5 of the nearest example; t_observed above null_mean means people show stronger similarity (numerical proximity) generalization than the model.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(sets)
    tgt = df["target"].astype(int).values
    d = np.empty(len(df))
    for i, k in enumerate(uniq):
        a = np.array([int(x) for x in k.split(",")])
        idx = codes == i
        d[idx] = np.abs(tgt[idx][:, None] - a[None, :]).min(axis=1)
    m = (d >= 1) & (d <= 5)
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].values[m].mean())
EOF
cat << 'EOF' > $D/parity_match_gap.py
# name: parity_match_gap
# description: Among sets whose examples share one parity (all even or all odd, >=2 examples), yes rate for targets matching that parity minus non-matching; t_observed above null_mean means people weight parity more than the model.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(sets)
    par = np.full(len(uniq), -1)
    for i, k in enumerate(uniq):
        a = np.array([int(x) for x in k.split(",")]) % 2
        if len(a) >= 2 and (a == a[0]).all():
            par[i] = a[0]
    p = par[codes]
    tp = df["target"].astype(int).values % 2
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    ok = p >= 0
    mt, mn = ok & (tp == p), ok & (tp != p)
    if mt.sum() == 0 or mn.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[mt].mean() - r[mn].mean())
EOF
cat << 'EOF' > $D/last_digit_share_yes_rate.py
# name: last_digit_share_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets sharing the last digit with at least one but not all examples (multi-example sets); t_observed above null_mean means people use partial surface-digit similarity the model's all-or-none rules ignore.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(sets)
    tgt = df["target"].astype(int).values
    m = np.zeros(len(df), dtype=bool)
    for i, k in enumerate(uniq):
        a = np.array([int(x) for x in k.split(",")])
        if len(a) < 2:
            continue
        idx = np.where(codes == i)[0]
        t = tgt[idx]
        sh = (t[:, None] % 10 == a[None, :] % 10)
        cnt = sh.sum(axis=1)
        notex = ~(t[:, None] == a[None, :]).any(axis=1)
        m[idx] = (cnt >= 1) & (cnt < len(a)) & notex
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].values[m].mean())
EOF
cat << 'EOF' > $D/per_set_yes_rate_sd.py
# name: per_set_yes_rate_sd
# description: Standard deviation across number_sets of each set's overall yes rate; t_observed above null_mean means people differentiate sets (tight vs broad concepts) more sharply than the model, below means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    g = df.groupby(df["number_set"].astype(str))["rating"].mean()
    if len(g) < 2:
        return 0.0
    return float(g.std())
EOF
ls $D; cd $D && python3 -c "
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, math, glob
df=pd.read_csv('/scr/wurgaft/auto-psych/agent_trees/fc3d1e4e3afb1c37/repo/_runs/cell_1/experiment1/model_loop/responses.csv')[['number_set','target','trial_index','rating']]
import time
for f in sorted(glob.glob('*.py')):
    g={'np':np,'pd':pd,'math':math}; exec(open(f).read(),g); t=time.time(); print(f, g['test_statistic'](df), round(time.time()-t,3))
"
